title: Jupiter-bound spacecraft gains 3.5 km/s using Earth’s gravity
content: On September 28, 2026, Juice, the Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer, accomplished a successful gravity assist flyby of Earth. This maneuver was pivotal in adjusting the spacecraft's trajectory and significantly boosting its speed without the need for extensive engine thrust. Throughout its mission, Juice has strategically employed gravity assists, effectively conserving fuel.

title: Elon Musk admits that Tesla Robotaxis have a 'cat problem'

However, it faces challenges with low-light detection, particularly struggling to identify small creatures like grey kittens in dark conditions. Elon Musk acknowledged the drawbacks of relying solely on cameras at a promotional event. In contrast, companies like Waymo incorporate various sensors, including lidar, to enhance their visibility.

title: Protester at Jantar Mantar takes bus key and flees; cops end up pushing vehicle

title: Bihar cop suspended after video shows him brandishing pistol at flood-hit people

He was filmed brandishing a pistol while distributing flood relief materials to affected citizens. The incident was widely circulated on social media, prompting an official statement from Saran's police department. title: Michigan collector paid $30 for painting; it later sold for record $1.35 million
content: In a stunning turn of events, Gertrude Abercrombie's painting, Alderman Merriam's Shells, was auctioned for $1,352,600 after being found at an estate sale for just $30. Having been lost for 75 years, the piece drew significant attention at Freeman's auction house, far exceeding expectations. A dedicated collector meticulously verified its authenticity, marking a remarkable resurgence for Abercrombie in the contemporary art scene.

title: California crews uncover 40-million-year-old mammal bones 12 feet underground
content: In a remarkable find during construction in Oceanside, California, fossilized remains were unearthed at a considerable depth. Expert paleontologist Joseph El Adli confirmed the identification of the bones, prompting a meticulous excavation effort. These fossils, dating back 40 to 45 million years from the Eocene Epoch, are under investigation to discern if they belong to brontotheres or amynodonts.

title: Illinois man built underground ‘caveman’ home in 1977; now listed for $59,000
content: An underground house located in Armington, Illinois, is currently on the market for $59,000. Built in the 1970s, the home features unique rock-lined interiors and circular windows. While the home offers significant size, much of the interior remains unfinished and requires renovation. Buyers should consider potential renovation costs alongside the low asking price per square foot. This property has potential for various uses, including a vacation home or rental.

title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
content: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan condemned the extensive deletion of voter names from electoral rolls due to the special intensive revision process. He emphasized that such actions undermine the core principles of the Indian Constitution and disenfranchise millions of citizens. Bhuyan highlighted that the right to vote is essential for free and fair elections in India. He urged that no citizen should be denied the right to vote without due process.

title: 3 years after Oct 7, Israel honours officer whose Hamas attack warning was ignored

Unfortunately, those alerts went unheeded, which led to a coordinated assault from Gaza, resulting in heavy casualties and numerous hostages. This incident has led to a critical examination of the systemic shortcomings within Israel's military intelligence operations.

title: Noida man held for 'molestation' at Kolkata hotel after Brazil match

Police reviewed CCTV footage and identified the accused, Palash Ray, in the hotel. Ray denied the allegations, claiming any contact was accidental, and investigations are ongoing. The statements of the victims and witnesses will be recorded as part of the inquiry.

title: The cancer risks you breathe, chew and drink
content: India faces significant cancer risks from tobacco, alcohol, and air pollution contributing to the disease prevalence. Smokeless tobacco products, such as gutkha and khaini, greatly increase oral cancer cases across the country. Alcohol consumption is recognized as a Group 1 carcinogen, associating with multiple cancer types beyond liver disease. Effective cancer prevention involves reducing exposure to these substances and promoting cleaner air.

title: Why Theodore Sturgeon’s 90% rule matters more in the age of AI
content: Sturgeon’s Law, often summarized as “90% of everything is crap,” was Theodore Sturgeon’s rhetorical response to critics who dismissed science fiction by highlighting its weakest examples. His broader point was that every creative field contains mediocre work, while its value lies in the strongest 10%. In today’s AI-driven publishing environment, the principle takes on new relevance as content becomes easier to produce and distribute. The challenge, therefore, is increasingly about finding worthwhile work rather than avoiding everything.

title: Bizarre! Ali Khan's wide ball goes for six, batter gets only five runs - Watch

Under MCC laws, a ball not hit by the bat counts as four, plus one for the wide. Toronto beat Mississauga Masters by nine runs and reached the final, where they will face Vancouver Anchors.

title: Mizoram woman left teaching for farming; now she is being honoured by UN

The current fleet consists of 29 fighter squadrons, much lower than the authorized strength. Efforts are underway to expedite the production of the Tejas Mark-1A and finalize the 114-aircraft Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft deal. Additionally, the Air Force is considering procuring fifth-generation fighters if domestic production experiences delays.

The company was ordered to refund Rs 88,000 and pay additional compensation and litigation costs. The manufacturer must comply within 45 days or face further financial penalties.
